learning_goal: Name every landmark on the upper end of the femur and the muscle attached to each, trace the retinacular blood supply of the head, and explain why an intracapsular fracture of the neck causes avascular necrosis while an intertrochanteric fracture does not.

terms: artery of the ligament of the head

structures.name: right femur
structures.label: Femur
structures.narration: The longest and strongest bone in the body. The upper end has four things to name: a head, a neck, and two trochanters. In front, the trochanters are joined by a rough intertrochanteric line; behind, by a sharper intertrochanteric crest that carries the quadrate tubercle.

structures.name: right hip bone
structures.label: Hip bone
structures.narration: The socket the head sits in, and the origin of most of the muscles that land on the trochanters. The obturator foramen below is where the obturator artery leaves the pelvis.

structures.label: Greater trochanter
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the CONTACT point where gluteus medius (FMA22330, gap 0.13 mm), gluteus minimus (FMA22332, 0.57 mm) and piriformis (FMA22340, 0.11 mm) converge on the femur — three witnesses scattered over 20.4 mm of a 440.2 mm bone (4.6%). Cross-checked against the most lateral point of the proximal 12% of the shaft, which lands at u=0.00, w=0.886: the same corner of the bone. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA24474 --contact FMA22330,FMA22332,FMA22340
structures.narration: The only part of the upper femur you can feel on a patient — the lateral bump about a hand's breadth below the iliac crest. Piriformis on its upper border, medius on its lateral surface, minimus in front.

structures.label: Trochanteric fossa
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the CONTACT point between the femur and obturator externus (FMA22326), gap 0.23 mm — one witness, no convergence check possible, because obturator externus is the only muscle that reaches the fossa. It sits medial to the greater trochanter anchor (u 0.358 vs 0.129) and at the same height (w 0.906 vs 0.933), which is where the fossa belongs. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA24474 --contact FMA22326
terms: medial side of the greater trochanter
structures.narration: The pit on the medial side of the greater trochanter. Obturator externus lands here, and nothing else does.

structures.label: Quadrate tubercle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the CONTACT point between the femur and quadratus femoris (FMA22338), gap 0.02 mm — one witness, but the tightest contact measured on this bone, and it is the most posterior of the four anchors (v 0.631), which is where the intertrochanteric crest runs. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA24474 --contact FMA22338
structures.narration: The rounded swelling at the midpoint of the intertrochanteric crest, behind. Quadratus femoris attaches here.

structures.label: Lesser trochanter
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the CONTACT point between the femur and psoas major (FMA22342), gap 0.87 mm — ONE witness, and the weakest of the four. Iliacus (FMA22322) was tried as a second witness and rejected: adding it scatters the pair over 77.8 mm (17.7% of the bone) and drags the mean to v=0.234, far anterior, because iliacus spreads down the front of the shaft below the trochanter. The psoas-only point sits just below and medial to the quadrate tubercle (w 0.774 vs 0.815), which is the correct relation. tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA24474 --contact FMA22342
structures.narration: Points backwards and medially. Iliopsoas alone attaches here, and it is that pull that flexes and externally rotates the shaft once the neck is broken.

structures.name: right gluteus medius
structures.label: Gluteus medius
structures.narration: Onto the oblique ridge on the lateral surface of the greater trochanter. It is the pull of this muscle and minimus that drags the greater trochanter upwards when the neck of the femur breaks.

structures.name: right gluteus minimus
structures.label: Gluteus minimus
structures.narration: Onto the front of the greater trochanter, just in front of medius.

structures.name: right piriformis
structures.label: Piriformis
structures.narration: Onto the very top of the greater trochanter — the highest attachment on the bone.

structures.name: right obturator internus
structures.label: Obturator internus
structures.narration: Onto the medial surface of the greater trochanter, with the two gemelli fused to its tendon above and below.

structures.name: right gemellus superior
structures.label: Gemellus superior
structures.narration: Blends with the tendon of obturator internus above.

structures.name: right gemellus inferior
structures.label: Gemellus inferior
structures.narration: Blends with the same tendon below.

structures.name: right obturator externus
structures.label: Obturator externus
structures.narration: Onto the trochanteric fossa, the pit on the medial side of the greater trochanter. Its tendon gets there by winding underneath the neck of the femur, and the medial circumflex femoral artery runs with it — which is why this muscle matters to the blood supply and not only to rotation.

structures.name: right quadratus femoris
structures.label: Quadratus femoris
structures.narration: Onto the quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest. The medial circumflex femoral artery reaches the back of the neck by passing between this muscle and obturator externus.

structures.name: right psoas major
structures.label: Psoas major
structures.narration: The tendon of psoas major is the whole reason the lesser trochanter exists. When the neck breaks, this muscle pulls the shaft up and rotates it outwards.

structures.name: right iliacus
structures.label: Iliacus
structures.narration: It joins the psoas tendon and spreads a little onto the bone below the lesser trochanter.

structures.name: right gluteus maximus
structures.label: Gluteus maximus
structures.narration: Only its deep lower quarter reaches the bone, at the gluteal tuberosity below the greater trochanter. The rest of the muscle stops at the iliotibial tract.

structures.name: right vastus lateralis
structures.label: Vastus lateralis
structures.narration: It arises from the lower edge of the greater trochanter and the outer lip of the linea aspera, wrapping the outside of the shaft. It is also the safe site for an intramuscular injection in a small child.

structures.name: right vastus medialis
structures.label: Vastus medialis
structures.narration: From the lower part of the intertrochanteric line, continuing down the medial lip of the linea aspera. Between them the two vasti show that the intertrochanteric line is a muscular attachment as well as the front edge of the joint capsule.

structures.name: right vastus intermedius
structures.label: Vastus intermedius
structures.narration: Straight off the front and side of the shaft, under the other two.

structures.name: right external iliac artery
structures.label: External iliac artery
structures.narration: This vessel becomes the femoral artery behind the inguinal ligament. The femoral gives off the profunda femoris, and the profunda gives off the two circumflex femoral arteries that supply the upper end of the femur. Follow the chain in that order and the blood supply of the head is easy to recite.

structures.name: right internal iliac artery
structures.label: Internal iliac artery
terms: artery of the ligament of the head
structures.narration: The obturator artery comes off this trunk, leaves the pelvis through the obturator foramen, and sends an acetabular branch along the ligament of the head. That is the second and smallest of the three sources of blood to the head, and the one that fails first.

structures.name: right external iliac vein
structures.label: External iliac vein
structures.narration: The femoral vein continues as this vessel. Worth knowing here because a fractured hip means immobility, and immobility in this venous system is how a fracture kills through pulmonary embolism rather than through the bone.

views.title: The upper end of the femur
views.narration: Everything in this scene is about the top few centimetres of one bone. Only one part of it can be felt on a patient: the greater trochanter, on the outside of the hip about a hand's breadth below the iliac crest. The head and neck are deep, and you find them by drawing lines rather than by touching them.

views.title: Name the landmarks
views.narration: From the top down: the head, smooth and spherical, with the fovea on its medial side. Then the neck, running down and out. Then the greater trochanter laterally and the lesser trochanter pointing backwards and medially — both marked here, and both measured on the bone rather than guessed. Joining them in front, the intertrochanteric line. Learn those six names — head, fovea, neck, greater trochanter, lesser trochanter, intertrochanteric line — before you learn anything attached to them. The two features that face backwards wait for the next beat.

views.title: The same bone from behind
views.narration: Turn it round, and the two features that were hidden a moment ago come into view. The intertrochanteric crest behind is sharper than the line in front, and carries the rounded quadrate tubercle at its midpoint — marked. Medial to the greater trochanter, between it and the neck, is the pit of the trochanteric fossa — also marked. Below the crest the gluteal tuberosity runs down into the linea aspera; that one is a roughening rather than a point, so it is named on the bone and not marked. The front and the back look different enough that a question can show you one view and expect you to say which it is.

views.title: Two angles that decide how the hip works
views.narration: The neck meets the shaft at about one hundred and twenty-five degrees in an adult, and it is also twisted about fifteen degrees forwards — anteversion, best seen from above like this. A smaller angle is coxa vara and shortens the limb; a larger one is coxa valga. In a child both angles are bigger, which is part of why children walk with their feet turned in.

views.title: Why the neck is built the way it is
views.narration: Cut the neck open. The bone inside is not solid: two systems of trabeculae cross each other, one running from the head down the medial side to resist compression, the other arching from the greater trochanter to resist tension. Where they cross is a dense strut called the calcar femorale; where they fail to overlap is a weak area, Ward's triangle. As bone is lost with age, Ward's triangle empties first, and that is where an elderly neck of femur gives way.

views.title: Where the blood comes from
views.narration: Two trunks feed this region. The external iliac becomes the femoral artery, gives the profunda femoris, and the profunda gives the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries. The internal iliac gives the obturator artery. Between them they supply the head three ways, and the three ways are very unequal.

views.title: The retinacular arteries — the supply that matters
views.narration: This is the path to learn. The medial circumflex femoral artery runs backwards between quadratus femoris and obturator externus, reaches the back of the neck, and there it breaks into small retinacular vessels that run up along the neck under the capsule, straight into the head. These supply most of the head in an adult. They are pressed against bone with nothing to protect them, so a fracture of the neck tears them.

views.title: The two supplies that cannot save the head
views.narration: The second source is the artery in the ligament of the head, traced here from the obturator artery. It is large in a child and often obliterated by adulthood, so it supplies only a small area around the fovea and cannot keep the head alive alone. The third is the nutrient supply coming up the shaft, which reaches the neck but rarely crosses into the head. So the head effectively depends on the retinacular vessels — a single supply with no useful backup.

views.title: Inside or outside the capsule
views.narration: The capsule attaches to the intertrochanteric line in front and only to the middle of the neck behind. A fracture medial to that attachment is intracapsular: it tears the retinacular vessels, the head loses its supply, and avascular necrosis follows in a large proportion of cases — so the head is usually replaced. A fracture through or below the trochanters is extracapsular: the vessels are outside the break, the bone unites, and it is fixed rather than replaced. One line on the bone, two completely different operations.

views.title: Why the broken leg lies short and turned out
views.narration: Once the neck is broken, nothing holds the shaft against the head, and the muscles simply pull. Iliopsoas drags the lesser trochanter up and rotates the shaft outwards; the gluteal abductors pull the greater trochanter up; the short rotators turn it further out. The result is the classic bedside picture — a shortened, externally rotated limb the patient cannot lift. You can now explain it muscle by muscle instead of memorising it.

views.title: Everything attached, in order
views.narration: Recite it by landmark. Greater trochanter: piriformis on top, gluteus medius laterally, minimus in front, obturator internus and the gemelli medially, obturator externus in the fossa behind. Intertrochanteric crest: quadratus femoris at the quadrate tubercle. Lesser trochanter: iliopsoas. Below them: gluteus maximus at the gluteal tuberosity and the vasti spreading over the shaft. Five landmarks, and every muscle of the buttock has an address on one of them.

gaps: The head, neck, greater trochanter, lesser trochanter, trochanteric fossa, intertrochanteric line and crest, quadrate tubercle and gluteal tuberosity are all sub-features of a single whole-femur mesh (FMA24474). FOUR of them are now measured landmark anchors — greater trochanter, trochanteric fossa, quadrate tubercle, lesser trochanter — each with its measurement in calibrated_by and each status 'needs-review'. Only the greater trochanter has more than one witness; the other three are single-contact measurements, which the tool reports as such.

Five features were NOT authored as anchors, and the reason is recorded so no later run re-derives them and believes the result. GLUTEAL TUBEROSITY: the contact with gluteus maximus (FMA22328) measures at w=0.630, a third of the way down the shaft, and at v=0.438 rather than posteriorly — the nearest point of that mesh to the bone is where its distal fibres lie against the shaft, not where its deep quarter inserts. The measurement is clean (gap 0.55 mm) and anatomically wrong, which is exactly the case an anchor must not be authored from. HEAD: the contact with the hip bone (gap 1.02 mm, u=0.664, w=0.977) is correct but marks a region, not a point, and the head needs no marker. FOVEA, INTERTROCHANTERIC LINE and INTERTROCHANTERIC CREST: each is a facet or a ridge, not a point, and neither of derive-landmark.mjs's two definitions — contact, extreme — describes a ridge. They stay named-on-the-bone.

The femoral artery, the profunda femoris and the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries have no models. The retinacular supply of the head — the single most examinable fact about this bone — is authored as a traced concept path from the external iliac artery through the plane between quadratus femoris and obturator externus onto the femur, with the named branches carried in narration.
The obturator artery and its acetabular branch have no models either, so the artery of the ligament of the head is traced as a concept from the internal iliac artery across the hip bone.

There is no ligament of the head of the femur, no capsule and no retinaculum in the catalog, so the capsular attachment that separates an intracapsular from an extracapsular fracture is shown with a relationship connector and a cut plane rather than as a surface.

Trabecular bone, the calcar femorale and Ward's triangle are internal architecture that a surface model cannot show. The cross-section beat cuts the outer shell and describes what a real section would reveal.
The trochanteric bursa has no model, so trochanteric bursitis is named but not shown.
This scene does not cover Hip joint, Sciatic nerve or Gluteal vessels. The hip bone and the two iliac vessels appear only as the frame and the parent trunks.
